task: Enable interactive user input in CodeMie agent chat: interactive elements (buttons, single/multi choice, validated short forms) in agent messages, agent pause/resume on explicit user input, and an 'Interactive features' assistant config block whose enabled-element catalog is exposed to the agent, across backend (codemie) and frontend (codemie-ui).

key_reasoning.reason: Cross-repo change (codemie backend + codemie-ui frontend) that modifies a shared contract in lockstep: the NDJSON StreamedGenerationResult stream schema (chains/base.py <-> chatGeneration.ts/_handleChunk) plus the assistant config schema (AssistantRequest <-> AssistantForm). Touches chat router/handlers, LangGraphAgent loop and event adapter, system-prompt/tool assembly for catalog exposure, Assistant SQLModel + migration, conversation persistence, and a new family of frontend interactive-element components.

Two genuinely novel areas: (1) agent-chat pause/resume — LangGraph interrupt/checkpoint primitives are installed and proven for workflows only, never wired into LangGraphAgent.stream()/assistant_handlers.py, and no agent-chat resume endpoint exists; (2) id-addressable interactive-element schema with post-action state updates, which the current text+Thought message model cannot persist. Zero test coverage exists for interactive elements, agent-chat interrupt/resume, or chunk-level stream parsing — exactly the areas this task touches — while text-only chat must not regress.

Technical analysis estimates ~10-15 backend files plus an alembic migration and ~15-20 frontend files (many new: Button, MultipleChoice, TextField, CheckBox, Column/Row/Text components, plus store, form, types, mock-server changes) — 25-35 files across many directories in two repositories.

All tiers of both applications: frontend UI/store/streaming client, backend API + handlers + service + agent runtime, DB persistence (assistants JSONB column migration and conversation message schema extension), and infrastructure (customer-config.yaml feature flag threaded through Helm ConfigMap). Cross-system by definition.

Acceptance criteria and the v1 element catalog are well specified, but the ticket's prescribed CopilotKit + AG-UI + A2UI stack has zero presence in either repo and structurally conflicts with the proprietary NDJSON protocol and the mandatory valtio-store architecture. The build-vs-adopt decision (adopt stack vs extend existing protocol with A2UI-style payloads) is an unmade architectural decision with major rework risk; message-persistence semantics for element state are also unspecified.

split_recommendation: Score 32/36 — splitting is mandatory before any planning. Suggested decomposition: (1) By dependency first — 'Interactive features' assistant config block end-to-end (JSONB column + migration + AssistantRequest sub-model + AssistantForm accordion + compareFormData + features:interactiveElements flag), a self-contained S/M story with the HedgingConfig precedent as an exact template; (2) By dependency second — agent-chat pause/resume infrastructure (LangGraph interrupt/checkpointer wired into LangGraphAgent.stream(), new resume endpoint, chatGeneration store resume handling), reusing the workflow-resume and EPMCDME-12393 plumbing; (3) By feature — action buttons happy path (simplest element: stream schema extension + Button rendering + structured action delivery + agent continue), the story that forces the protocol/build-vs-adopt decision; (4) By feature — MultipleChoice single/multi; (5) By feature — short forms with client-side validation (required/regex/email) + Submit; (6) By phase last — element state persistence and post-action state updates (conversation.py schema extension, history materialization, id-addressable element updates surviving reload). A preceding spike/ADR story to decide protocol-extension vs CopilotKit/AG-UI adoption is strongly recommended before story 3.
